topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, reviews prior lecture context, and outlines the learning outcomes regarding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptor pathways and downstream cascades confer growth signal autonomy and resistance to inhibitory signals in cancer cells.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how blocks in terminal differentiation prevent cells from exiting the cell cycle and contribute to tumorigenesis in hematopoietic tissues and colonic epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through the disruption of p53 signaling and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss telomere biology, mechanisms of telomerase reactivation, and how bypassing senescence and p53-mediated stress responses allows cancer cells to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex hallmarks and explain how metabolic reprogramming, aerobic glycolysis, and oncometabolites support tumor growth and epigenetic alteration.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and the role of new blood vessel formation in providing oxygen and nutrients to sustain growing tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cells, seed-and-soil interactions, and the genomic features underlying distant tumor colonization.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of cancer hallmarks, reflections on recent literature, and final reminders for practical sessions.
